command_site_revisions.what: the site no longer resolves its own frozen round (status:'active', sort -created_date, limit 1). It consumes loadRoundContext and refuses BEFORE any write when the contract reports conflict 'multiple_active_rounds'; the round's ballots are read from the same context (ctx.ballots) instead of a second independent query.
command_site_revisions.why: with two active rounds the site bound a ballot to whichever round the sort put first, while issuance and the governed read REFUSE that same state — so a ballot could be recorded against an electorate no package may be issued from (silent orphan vote + false 'has voted' state). See D-039 / reference R-17.
command_site_revisions.kernel_impact: NONE — no module digest above changed, so this does not by itself invalidate the authority/integrity/eligibility unit evidence; the three suites were re-run anyway (PASS).
command_site_revisions.coverage_gap: no suite exercises the CastVote HANDLER: the round contract's own cases pass (incl. two active rounds => no round chosen), but the site behaviour is verified by source + build + module suites only.

command_site_revisions.what: the decision state chain is read from ONE contract (shared/decisionLifecycle.ts) at every material transition: open_vote accepts draft|proposed, cast_vote and close_vote accept voting only, and issue accepts approved for a FIRST issuance while issued|executing take the idempotent answer (code already_issued).
command_site_revisions.why: the chain was declared in more than one place and the declarations disagreed: CreateDecisionDraft writes 'draft' and nothing writes 'proposed', so OpenVote — which accepted only voting|proposed — made the positive cycle unreachable (D-041); and IssueDecision accepted seven states including draft|proposed while refusing with 'must be approved', so approval, issuance and effectiveness were not distinguished.
command_site_revisions.policy_choice_made: the RECOMMENDED option was applied (widen the open-vote gate to accept a governed draft) rather than adding a state no command writes. Both were policy choices; this one adds no unreachable state.
command_site_revisions.kernel_impact: NONE — no kernel digest changed, so the kernel version string stays authz-1.2.0-rc.2 (which the running suite reports). A NEW command-site policy source (decisionLifecycle.ts) is recorded above, marked added_after the rc.2 freeze. What this change invalidates is evidence about the decision/vote PATHS, not about the kernel.
command_site_revisions.coverage_gap: no suite exercises the HANDLERS: TestDecisionLifecycle asserts the contract object the handlers consume, not a handler, a persisted decision or a deployment.

command_site_revisions.what: four governed commands replace direct browser writes on the meeting surfaces, each reading its states and its right from meeting-lifecycle-1.0.0: agenda stages (agenda.edit prepares · agenda.approve closes · closure requires a COMPUTED readiness), withdrawal instead of deletion (agenda.edit), minutes content with SERVER-side text policy and only while the minutes can still be corrected (minutes.draft), and the minutes steps that had no command at all (minutes.draft submit · minutes.issue release · minutes.review amend).
command_site_revisions.why: the agenda stage, the removal of an item and the minutes text were written straight from the browser with no command: a surface could assert a decision the committee never took, a record could be DELETED (a governance record that can be deleted cannot be audited), and the authority on what entered a governance document was the browser. The three minutes steps and the governed content write did not exist at all (D-019, D-020, D-022, D-024).
command_site_revisions.kernel_impact: SECURITY — this is the revision that moved the guard's state lists into the contracts and named minutes.issue, so the kernel version moved to authz-1.3.0 and prior evidence is invalidated. The suites were re-run against it.
command_site_revisions.coverage_gap: no suite exercises these HANDLERS: TestMeetingLifecycle asserts the contract and the text policy they consume, not a handler, a meeting or a deployment. The repository's own static checker (scripts/authority-guardrails.mjs) could NOT be executed from the builder environment; its six rules were applied to the new files by inspection instead (no client-supplied role, no client organisation in the guard, no name-based identity match, no fail-open authority, no read capability gating a write, trusted target on every write).
